taxonomic_note: Accepted at species rank. Central Texas material is often treated regionally as var. grandiflora; that name is retained as infraspecific/historical context, not a duplicate learner taxon.
look_here_first: Find narrow cauline leaves and the long, loose blue-flowering axis. Flip to a flower CALYX: the green 15-ribbed surface (local var. grandiflora treatment) remains visible between short hairs/glands, unlike the dense white OR violet felt covering S. farinacea calyces. Check flower cluster spacing, not petal blue color alone.
project_tracker_diagnostic: Tall perennial with narrow opposite linear-lanceolate leaves, long open terminal flowering axis, and green ribbed hairy calyces lacking the farinose/mealy coating of S. farinacea.

project_inclusion.range_basis: 2026-10-14 corrected two-county status: Hays, Travis inside 24-county zone; Williamson outside. Third accepted native county not yet established. Original evidence retained in range_audit.

range_audit.confidence: high for target-zone membership; historic county-locality citations retained, not independently re-vouchered
range_audit.reason: Third project county not actually verified. Does not mean native absence from other target counties.
range_audit.original_range_basis: Hays County native inventory, Travis County preserve/herbarium records, and UT Williamson County treatment; no county presence inferred.

morphology_keys.habit: Woody-rootstock herbaceous perennial, often upright; not a rosette. Central Texas local treatment often below 1 m.
morphology_keys.leaves: UT Texas var. grandiflora: only cauline leaves, narrow linear-lanceolate to linear-oblanceolate ~30–80 × 4–8 mm, mostly entire/subentire.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Long, open interrupted panicle of paired axillary cymes; lower part sometimes leafy; often only 1 flower of each cyme open at a time.
morphology_keys.calyx: Green-surfaced, bell-shaped, ~8 mm long and ca. 15-ribbed (UT local variety treatment), short-hairy with glandular hairs but not densely felted like S. farinacea.
morphology_keys.variety_caution: Central Texas azure sage often var. grandiflora. New Alex Abair close photograph is Florida var. azurea; retain variety/provenance label, do not equate to local material.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Mealy blue sage has a conspicuously mealy/felted calyx. Engelmann sage is a low dense clump with strongly glandular foliage and compact flowering architecture.

curation_status.visual_status: 2 new exact species image downloads staged, including Texas flower and Florida variety-level study calyx; arrows/ruler macros remain.

photo_comparison_lesson.memory_rule: Azure = narrow leaves + airy axis + exposed green calyx; Mealy = broader toothed leaves + crowded axis + white-or-violet felted calyx.
photo_comparison_lesson.look_here_first: Inspect the CALYX behind a blue flower first; use dense hair coat, leaf blades and flowering-axis spacing together.

diagnostic_differences.azurea: Green surface normally exposed, approx 15 ribs, short hairs and stalked glands
diagnostic_differences.farinacea: Heavily felted in white or dark violet hairs, roughly 10-ribbed, calyx flattened

diagnostic_differences.azurea: Narrow typically 4–8 mm wide, mostly entire

cautions: Dark violet farinacea calyx still counts as MEALY; lack of white is not evidence of azurea.
Azurea calyces are themselves hairy; presence of any hair is not species proof.
S. azurea var. azurea nonlocal photos are comparative study only for local grandiflora.
